immunohistochemistry for LAMP-1 and adipophilin can be used to differentiate phospholipopidosis and hepatic lipidosis, respectively.
immunohistochemical detection of LAMP-2 is a useful method to identify cytoplasmic phospholipid vacuolation, while adipophilin is useful in identifying nonphospholipid vacoulation.

the development of a rapid and reliable diagnostic tool to differentiate phospholypidosis and lipid accumulation in the liver of rats.
the development of a rapid, simple and reliable immunohistochemical method for the identification of lipidosis and phospholipid in the liver of rats.
developing a simple, rapid, sensitive method to differentiate hepatic lipidosis from hepatic phospholipid in the liver of rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LAMP-2 immunohistochemical stains are more sensitive than electron microscopy for the diagnosis of phospholiposis and that adipophilin immunohistochemical stain are more sensitive than Oil Red-O for the diagnosis of lipidosis.

LAMP-2 staining can be used to differentiate phospholipopidosis from other vacuolating lesions and adipophilin staining can be used for the differentiation of lipidosis from other vacuo-lating lesions.
the LAMP-2 and adipophilin immunohistochemical stains are useful in the differentiation of hepatic lipidosis from hepatic phospholipid in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

LAMP-2 and adipophilin immunohistochemical stainings can be utilized to differentiate hepatic phospholipid accumulation (phospholipid storage disease) from non-phosphorylated lipid accumulation (fatty liver) in rat livers.
LAMP-2 and adipophilin immunohistochemistry is a useful adjunct to the light microscopic evaluation of hepatic cytoplasmic vacuoles in rats.
immunohistochemical methods for LAMP- 2 and adipophilin can be used to differentiate between nonphosphorylative lipidosis and phospholipidotic vacuolation in the liver of rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that

immunohistochemical detection of LAMP-2 can be used to diagnose phospholipid accumulation in the liver and that the presence of adipophilin can be used to differentiate non-phosphorylated lipid accumulation.
the use of immunostaining for LAMP-1 and/or adipophilin can be used to differentiate hepatic phospholipid accumulation from hepatic lipid accumulation in the livers from rats.
the use of immunostaining for LAMP-1/2 and adipophilin is a rapid and sensitive method to differentiate between lipidosis and phospholipid in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded liver tissue.
